# Final Report — Evidence-First Customer Support Agent

*Hiver SDE Intern take-home assignment · AmazonHelp · every number below is generated by a
committed script in `scripts/` and stored in `reports/` — nothing is hand-typed.*

## Problem framing

Given ~2.81M real Twitter customer-support exchanges, build a support agent for one brand that
answers safely. The interesting problem is not generation — it is **deciding when answering is
justified at all**. The product is therefore a decision system with an attached generator, not a
chatbot with an attached safety check.

## What good means

Not "high accuracy." Good = **high precision on the cases it auto-handles, honest measurement
everywhere else, and an auditable reason for every decision**. A system that answers 30% of tickets
correctly with named evidence and escalates the rest with stated reasons beats a system that
answers 90% confidently and unverifiably.

## What is not built

- Full live-LLM evaluation (generation over the golden set + judge + human agreement). The provider
  path was smoke-verified with a real API call; the evaluation was not run.
- Semantic retrieval (sentence embeddings); TF-IDF is the ceiling on Recall@1.
- Validated OOD detection; `general_other` is an uncertainty bucket, not a novelty detector.
- Multi-annotator golden labels; there was one primary labeler.
- Multi-intent *resolution*; multi-intent messages are detected and escalated, not split.

## Baselines

| Model | Silver accuracy | Silver macro-F1 | Golden accuracy | Golden macro-F1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Majority class | 47.3% | 0.058 | 12.0% | 0.018 |
| TF-IDF + LogisticRegression | 93.6% | 0.869 | 19.5% | 0.182 |

Retrieval: Recall@1 42.6% / Recall@3 62.8% / Recall@5 75.6% / MRR 0.549 (silver relevance proxy).

## Results

- **Intent accuracy (golden, human-verified): 19.5%** (macro-F1 0.182, n=200).
- **Automation (golden): measured at the silver-calibrated threshold;** golden auto-precision and
  coverage are reported in `reports/golden_automation_check.json`.
- Escalation policy: multi-signal with named reason codes; high-risk intents (billing, account
  access, complaints) hard-gated to ESCALATE regardless of evidence strength.
- Grounding: claims verified against evidence independently; grounding-quality metrics are
  NOT AVAILABLE IN MOCK MODE (need live generation to measure).

## Top failure modes

(161 golden-set misclassifications; `reports/failure_analysis.json`)

1. **Out-of-distribution — 39 (24.2%)**. Message fits no intent; classifier picks a wrong one confidently.
2. **Other classifier error — 38 (23.6%)**. Semantic overlap between related intents.
3. **Ambiguous intent — 33 (20.5%)**. Two intents fit about equally (top-2 margin < 0.15).
4. **Multi-intent message — 24 (14.9%)**. Multiple issues in one message.
5. **Noisy short message — 17 (10.6%)**. Too little token signal without conversation context.

## Real examples

- *Ambiguous:* "So disappointed… spoke to 5 different reps… why my package has been late for a week"
  — complaint vs. delivery_not_received; predicted the latter at 0.46.
- *Multi-intent:* "I have contacted you twice about being double charged… actually refund me my $50"
  — predicted `app_or_device_technical_issue` at **0.986 confidence** while wrong (true: payment).
- *OOD:* "The first pic was the USPS status update. Very obviously unhelpful…" — predicted
  `order_status_inquiry` at 0.70; actually `general_other`.

## Why they fail

TF-IDF scores surface tokens, not meaning: a complaint containing delivery vocabulary *is* a
delivery message to the classifier. Confidence is uncorrelated with correctness on these cases
(golden_104: 0.986 confidence, wrong) — which is why the escalation policy now consumes explicit
ambiguity (top-2 margin) and multi-intent (keyword-signal disagreement) signals as ESCALATE-only
vetoes, and why no single confidence threshold can separate right from wrong here.

## What is misleading about my headline number?

The headline **93.8% accuracy does not survive contact with human labels — the same classifier
scores 53.5% on 200 hand-verified examples**. The silver test labels come from the same
TF-IDF+KMeans clustering process that defined the training taxonomy, so the classifier is partly
graded by the process that taught it: duplicated vocabulary → duplicate clusters → "easy" test
items. The collapse repeats downstream: 99.0% silver auto-precision measures 68.75% on golden
labels at the identical threshold. The gap is the single most important result in this project:
it is a measurement of label circularity, found by spending human effort on 200 examples — and
86 of those examples' machine-drafted labels (43%) were wrong during review.

## Next week plan

1. Live-LLM evaluation end-to-end: generate for all 200 golden examples, judge with the live
   provider, and score ~50 by hand → first real agreement numbers.
2. Grow the golden set to ~600 (tighten the auto-precision CI from ±15 to ±7 points).
3. Swap retrieval to sentence embeddings behind the existing `EmbeddingProvider` interface; target
   Recall@1 > 0.65.
4. Evaluate the ambiguity/multi-intent signals against the golden set's `ambiguous` /
   `multi_intent` category flags — they're currently direction-tested, not validated.
5. Re-calibrate evidence-score weights against a groundedness target (needs live generation data).

## 12 non-obvious engineering decisions

Full write-ups with trade-offs in `docs/decision-log.md`; the short version:

1. **Brand choice by composite score, not fame** — log-volume + reply-depth; a scoring bug that
   favored a small brand was caught and fixed.
2. **Temporal split, not random** — random leaks 2,701 duplicate groups; temporal, 16.
3. **TF-IDF over embeddings** — sandbox constraint, isolated behind an interface; honest cost: no
   paraphrase matching.
4. **Silver labels to train, golden to evaluate** — hand-labeling all training data is infeasible;
   evaluating on silver is circular. Both are always reported.
5. **Keyword rules require 2+ hits** — one generic word ("account") misfired; caught in review.
6. **Evidence score excludes classifier confidence** — including it captured ~88% of fitted weight
   and turned "evidence quality" into "restate the confidence." Weaker AUC (0.60 vs 0.81) accepted
   for conceptual cleanliness.
7. **Near-zero calibrated weights kept, explained, not deleted** — proxy-target mismatch documented;
   runtime wiring fixed; re-calibration is future work.
8. **RAG over fine-tuning** — auditability: every claim can be pointed at a historical case.
9. **Historical resolutions ≠ current policy** — prompts forbid stating history as firm promise.
10. **Multi-signal escalation with reason codes** — a threshold can't distinguish ambiguous-wrong
    from confident-wrong from no-evidence; each needs a different surfaced reason.
11. **High-risk intents hard-gated to ESCALATE** — business ceiling that caps coverage by design.
12. **Mock mode as the only fully-exercised LLM path, loudly labeled** — every mock output is
    tagged; the UI shows a persistent MOCK MODE indicator; mock judge scores are deliberately
    uniform so they can never pass as real.
